A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JOLT-SQL research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original Spider/BIRD experiments, schema-linking evaluations, component ablations, training and inference timings, and a model-output case study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds cross-dataset evaluations and reduced-training-data experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The discriminative schema linker, local bidirectional attention, selective attention, joint loss, confusion-aware sampling with first-epoch caching, and inference procedure are unchanged. The added experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds evaluations on Spider-Syn, Spider-Realistic, Spider-DK, and KaggleDBQA. This substantially extends coverage beyond the original Spider/BIRD evaluations to additional robustness variants and transfer to unseen databases and query types.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments. RSL-SQL is newly mentioned in the baseline paragraph but already appeared in v1 Table 1. New Tables 8–9 report only JOLT-SQL configurations.

E3.justification: Added protocols evaluate Spider-trained models on transfer datasets and vary 7B training data through 5%, 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100%. Existing metrics, hyperparameters, and greedy decoding remain unchanged. Section 4.1 broadens its Dev/Test wording, but no BIRD Test scores establish additional test-set use.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 add two substantive analysis directions: generalization of Spider-trained models to shifted or unseen datasets, and sensitivity to reduced annotation availability. These extend the existing component ablations, threshold analysis, and noisy-schema case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 8–9 add substantial transfer and data-efficiency result sets. For example, KaggleDBQA EX is 47.0/52.4 for 7B/14B, while 7B trained on 5% of the data achieves 81.9 Spider Dev EX and 54.0 BIRD Dev EX. Existing Tables 1–7 and threshold-plot results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged, including the attention sets, losses, and sampling rule. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about single-stage joint training, confusion-aware robustness, competitive execution accuracy, and efficiency. The headline performance claims and contribution scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new appendix sections interpret the added results as evidence of cross-dataset generalization and graceful degradation with less training data. Appendix A.1 adds an explanation attributing efficiency to shared training passes. The stated model-scale and implementation-complexity limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly discloses exclusive use of the respective training sets, and Table 6 adds an approximate A30 instance cost of $0.18 per hour. Existing implementation details remain stable. The displayed code-link text changes, but its embedded destination is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds four dataset-related references: Deng et al. (2021), Gan et al. (2021a, 2021b), and Lee et al. (2021). The main related-work discussion and positioning against prompting and SFT methods remain unchanged; other reference edits principally update bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: There are limited edits to author contact information, code-link wording, the setup and baseline descriptions, and the ablation explanation. Two Appendix A subsections are added, while the main narrative and existing section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9, enlarges Table 1, relocates Figure 4 and appendix displays, and renumbers the hyperparameter table from 8 to 10. Figure 6 adds green highlighting to address_id in both SQL outputs without changing the example or findings.

improvement.justification: Appendices A.2–A.3 provide useful transfer and reduced-data evidence absent from v1, while the enlarged main table and added training/cost disclosures improve presentation and documentation. The gain is limited: the new experiments lack matched comparator results, uncertainty estimates, and subset-selection details. They strengthen support for the existing method without substantially changing its validation quality.
